clinical_category: Chronic respiratory disease adjustment - ongoing psychosocial assessment and support
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial assessment, coping support, and resource coordination during chronic illness
stem: A client with chronic respiratory disease says, "I have stopped seeing friends because the illness has changed so much of my life, and I feel down most days." Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Assess mood, coping, safety, social functioning, and support needs; provide ongoing emotional support and coordinate appropriate pulmonary-rehabilitation, social-work, or mental-health resources
options.B: Limit follow-up to medication adherence because psychosocial concerns no longer require assessment once respiratory treatment is stable
options.C: Explain that social withdrawal is an expected consequence of chronic lung disease and does not require further evaluation
options.D: Wait until the client specifically requests psychiatric treatment before acknowledging mood or adjustment concerns

rationale: A is correct. Current American Thoracic Society pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance defines rehabilitation as a comprehensive, patient-tailored intervention intended to improve both physical and psychological condition in chronic respiratory disease. ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation resources explicitly include psychosocial support within integrated care. Current NCBI/StatPearls pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance likewise emphasizes that progressive lung disease has important psychological and social effects, that anxiety and depression should be assessed, and that psychologists and social workers may be incorporated when needed. B, C, and D dismiss clinically meaningful mood, coping, and social-function changes that warrant assessment and individualized support.
educational_objective: Support psychological adjustment to chronic respiratory disease through ongoing assessment of mood, coping, safety, and social functioning and by coordinating individualized psychosocial and rehabilitation resources rather than assuming emotional needs end when medical treatment stabilizes.
source_organization: American Thoracic Society (ATS), corroborated by National Library of Medicine (NCBI Bookshelf/StatPearls)
source_document_title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Adults with Chronic Respiratory Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline; Pulmonary Rehabilitation
source_version_date: Official ATS clinical practice guideline published 2023 and currently listed by ATS in 2026; StatPearls Pulmonary Rehabilitation current 2026 Internet edition accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: ATS Pulmonary Rehabilitation guideline/implementation resources → pulmonary rehabilitation is a comprehensive patient-tailored intervention designed to improve physical and psychological condition in chronic respiratory disease; current ATS Pulmonary Rehabilitation Assembly scope includes psychosocial support as part of integrated care. NCBI Bookshelf 'Pulmonary Rehabilitation' → Personnel/Psychosocial Support: progressive advanced lung disease has psychological and social effects; anxiety and depression should be addressed; psychologists and social workers may be involved; education and psychosocial support are important components of comprehensive care.
source_claim_supported: Current ATS and NCBI resources directly support integrating ongoing psychological and social assessment and support into chronic respiratory-disease care and using multidisciplinary rehabilitation or mental-health resources when indicated.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests assessment of mood and coping, therapeutic support, social functioning, and coordination of psychosocial resources in chronic illness.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The original generic ATS homepage and vague 'ongoing emotional support' wording were replaced with current ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance and an exact NCBI psychosocial-support locator. The final item tests a concrete nursing response to mood and social-withdrawal concerns and remains distinct from V2-Q1948, which tests the anxiety-breathlessness interaction.
audit_findings: The original ATS root URL did not provide an exact psychosocial-support locator.
Current ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation guidance explicitly targets both physical and psychological condition in chronic respiratory disease and maintains psychosocial support within integrated care.
Current NCBI/StatPearls content directly supports assessment and treatment of anxiety/depression and multidisciplinary psychological/social-work involvement when indicated.
The final construct is distinct from V2-Q1948 by testing chronic mood/social-adjustment assessment rather than acute anxiety during dyspnea.

Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely appropriate answer, no second defensible option, no unsupported claim that every client requires formal psychotherapy, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
